narrow: The unconditional return assertion is false on an infeasible member of \(\mathfrak C_{1}\): if no protocol individually certifies some factor, then \(\operatorname{Opt}=+\infty\) and no accepted certificate can be returned. The proposed claim retains exact equivalence, including the infeasible case, and adds the necessary condition \(\operatorname{Opt}<+\infty\) only to the greedy-return clause.

verdict.note: Accept both approval items. `thm:explicit-oracle-enumeration-frontier` faithfully optimizes the already defined class of uniform certificates accepted by `Acc`; it neither assumes nor claims the unresolved conversion from arbitrary acquired collections to uniform certificates. Exhaustive protocol/label/branch enumeration, at most 2^m oracle queries, k<=L, and subset dynamic programming justify the stated 2^{O(m+L)} upper bound; canonical-certificate tie-breaking can be retained within the same bound. `lem:known-one-action-cover-corollary` is a correctness-preserving narrowing: it handles infeasibility explicitly, preserves exact optimum equality, and conditions certificate-return and the H_k guarantee on finite optimum. Its load-bearing no-synergy and protocolwise-legality premises are already explicit restrictions of C_1, not hidden assumptions or novelty claims.
